questions.q: Define "digital footprint" and distinguish between active and passive digital footprints with one example each.
questions.a: A digital footprint is the trail of data created by a user's online activities. Active digital footprint: data intentionally submitted (e.g., posting a photo on Instagram). Passive digital footprint: data collected without explicit user action (e.g., website recording IP address and browsing history via cookies). A wrong answer that confuses the two (e.g., calling cookies "active" because user "chose" to visit the site) reveals misunderstanding of intentionality — passive footprints are generated by system-level tracking, not user consent.

questions.q: A student downloads a 2-minute educational video from YouTube, adds a title slide "Prepared by [Student Name]", and submits it as their own project work. Is this plagiarism, copyright infringement, both, or neither? Explain using the definitions from the NCERT textbook.
questions.a: This is both plagiarism and copyright infringement. Plagiarism: presenting someone else's work (the video content) as one's own by adding a false attribution. Copyright infringement: using the video without permission from the copyright holder (YouTube's Terms of Service and the creator's rights), even if modified. A wrong answer claiming "fair use" or "only plagiarism" reveals confusion between ethical attribution (plagiarism) and legal permission (copyright) — the NCERT explicitly states that giving reference does not make copyrighted material free to use.

questions.q: Your friend receives an SMS: "Your ATM card ending in 4567 will be blocked. Update KYC immediately: http://sbi-kyc-update.tk". They are about to click the link. List three specific technical indicators in this message that confirm it is a phishing attempt, and state the immediate action they should take.
questions.a: Three indicators: (1) URL uses .tk (free Tokelau domain) instead of sbi.co.in or onlinesbi.com; (2) URL path "kyc-update" is not a standard SBI endpoint; (3) SMS creates urgency ("immediately", "will be blocked") — a social engineering tactic. Immediate action: Do not click; delete the SMS; report to bank's official helpline (not the number in SMS) and forward to 1930 (India's cyber crime helpline). A wrong answer focusing only on "spelling errors" or "unknown sender" misses the technical domain analysis that is definitive proof.

questions.q: Compare ethical hacking and non-ethical hacking across four dimensions: intent, authorisation, outcome, and legal status. Provide one real-world example of each.
questions.a: Ethical hacking: intent = improve security; authorisation = explicit written permission; outcome = vulnerabilities reported and fixed; legal = legal under IT Act. Example: Company hires certified ethical hacker (CEH) to penetration-test their web app. Non-ethical hacking: intent = steal data/disrupt services; authorisation = none; outcome = data breach, financial loss; legal = criminal offence under IT Act Sections 43, 66. Example: Attacker exploits SQL injection to steal customer database. A wrong answer that equates "technical skill" with ethics reveals the misconception that hacking is defined by technique rather than authorisation and intent.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Using a strong password is sufficient to protect your social media account from being compromised." Support your evaluation with at least three distinct attack vectors that bypass password strength.
questions.a: The statement is false. Three attack vectors bypassing password strength: (1) Phishing: user voluntarily enters password on fake login page; (2) Session hijacking: attacker steals session cookie after legitimate login; (3) SIM swapping: attacker ports victim's phone number to intercept 2FA codes; (4) Keylogger malware: records keystrokes including strong password; (5) Credential stuffing: reused password from another breached site. A wrong answer claiming "strong password prevents all attacks" reveals the misconception that authentication security is single-factor; defence-in-depth (2FA, device trust, phishing awareness) is essential.

questions.q: Give the correct order of immediate actions after receiving a suspicious bank-verification email asking for your PIN.
questions.a: The response runs: (1) Inspect the sender domain against the bank's real domain (2) Refuse to click the link or enter the PIN anywhere (3) Delete the message and report it through the bank's official helpline (4) Forward the details to the national cyber crime helpline. A wrong answer that clicks first to check shows the student has missed that phishing exploits trust and urgency, and that technical indicators must be verified before any action.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Cyber safety refers to the practices, measures, and awareness required to protect individuals, systems, and networks from cyber threats such as ______ access, data theft, malware, phishing, and identity theft, while ensuring ethical, legal, and responsible use of digital technologies.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you receive an email ______ to be from your bank asking you to "verify your account" by clicking a link and entering your PIN.
What is Cyber safety? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Cyber safety refers to the practices, measures, and awareness required to protect individuals, systems, and networks from cyber threats such as unauthorised access, data theft, malware, phishing, and identity theft, while ensuring ethical, legal, and responsible use of digital technologies.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Cyber safety?
questions.a: Students believe that "deleting a post or photo from social media permanently removes it from the internet." This misconception arises because the UI shows the content disappearing from their profile, creating a false sense of control.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to classify a given online scenario into the correct cyber threat category (hacking, phishing, identity theft, ransomware, cyber bullying, plagiarism, copyright infringement) and justify the classification using at least two specific indicators from the scenario.
